taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes competing generic arrangements for American ranids (Lithobates used here).
fieldMarks: Large: 3.25-4.63 in snout-vent (record 6.13 in); greenish-black back.
Light spots on the lips, larger on the lower jaw.
Skin more rugose than most ranid frogs; no dorsolateral ridges.
Belly grey to almost black with light spots or short wavy lines; males often have yellowish throat.
Webbing on hind feet reaches the last phalanx of the longest toe.
behavior: Highly aquatic and approachable; sits in shallow open water and on logs.
Eats insects and other invertebrates, occasionally small vertebrates including other ranid frogs.
habitat: Swamps along streams and edges of shallow ponds and impoundments, including beaver ponds; open, thinly vegetated shorelines.
range: Coastal Plain from southern North Carolina (at least formerly) to northern Florida and west to southeastern Mississippi; most of the range is in northern Florida, southern Georgia and southern South Carolina.
